events.title: Han astronomers record China's first precisely dated sunspot
events.description: During the reign of Emperor Cheng of Han, Chinese astronomers made the first precisely dated sunspot observation in China. The astronomer Gan De of the State of Qi had recognised sunspots as solar phenomena in the 4th century BCE.
events.html: During the reign of Emperor Cheng of Han, Chinese astronomers made the first precisely dated sunspot observation in China. The astronomer Gan De of the State of Qi had recognised sunspots as solar phenomena in the 4th century BCE.

events.title: Agapetus II becomes pope as the nominee of Alberic II of Spoleto
events.description: Alberic II, princeps of Rome from 932 to 954, controlled the papacy and appointed the five popes after John XI, among them Agapetus II. The new pontificate fell in the period known as the Saeculum obscurum.

events.title: Temür is enthroned as the second emperor of the Yuan dynasty
events.description: Temür, known by his temple name as the Emperor Chengzong of Yuan, reigned until 10 February 1307. He is counted as the sixth Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, though only nominally, as the empire was divided; his reign set the patterns of power for decades.

events.title: Columbus sights the Cayman Islands
events.description: On his fourth voyage, Christopher Columbus sighted two small islands teeming with turtles, which he named Las Tortugas. They later became known as the Cayman Islands.

events.title: Parliament passes the Tea Act
events.description: The Act let the East India Company ship tea directly to America, undercutting smugglers while keeping the Townshend duty. Colonists saw it as a ploy to make them accept taxation, leading to the Boston Tea Party.
events.html: The Act let the East India Company ship tea directly to America, undercutting smugglers while keeping the Townshend duty. Colonists saw it as a ploy to make them accept taxation, leading to the Boston Tea Party.

events.title: Second Continental Congress meets in Philadelphia
events.description: Delegates from the colonies gathered weeks after Lexington and Concord. The Congress created the Continental Army, appointed George Washington to command it and declared independence in 1776.

events.title: Stonewall Jackson dies of pneumonia
events.description: Eight days after being wounded by his own men at Chancellorsville, General Thomas 'Stonewall' Jackson died. Lee said he had lost his right arm.
events.html: Eight days after being wounded by his own men at Chancellorsville, General Thomas 'Stonewall' Jackson died. Lee said he had lost his right arm.

events.title: Union cavalry capture Jefferson Davis in Georgia
events.description: The fleeing Confederate president was seized near Irwinville, Georgia. He was held for two years at Fort Monroe but never brought to trial.
events.html: The fleeing Confederate president was seized near Irwinville, Georgia. He was held for two years at Fort Monroe but never brought to trial.

events.title: Golden spike completes the first transcontinental railroad
events.description: The Central Pacific and Union Pacific lines met at Promontory Summit, Utah. Coast-to-coast travel fell from months to about a week, at great cost to Native American lands.

events.title: Churchill becomes Prime Minister as Germany attacks in the West
events.description: As German forces invaded the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg, Neville Chamberlain resigned and Winston Churchill formed a coalition government to lead Britain's war.
events.html: As German forces invaded the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg, Neville Chamberlain resigned and Winston Churchill formed a coalition government to lead Britain's war.

song: German Christians of the late Middle Ages; later Lutheran churches and English-speaking choirs
A Christmas carol from about 1328 that mixes German and Latin. A story says its writer heard angels sing it and danced with them.
